summary: Menominee County, WI tower that FFLA and a second Wisconsin list show as standing; no build date, owner or history found in the sources reached.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Sand Lake (W) in Menominee County as a standing tower at the stated coordinates
FFLA tells the two Sand Lake towers apart with the letters (P) and (W)
a second list places a Sand Lake tower in Menominee County, with no other detail
WJFW reports Wisconsin's 72 towers were decommissioned in 2015
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: the DNR plan covered the 72 towers, mostly in northern Wisconsin, to be taken out of service in 2016
evidence.quote: Seventy-two fire towers (mostly in Northern Wisconsin) used by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR), including five in Sawyer County, will be taken out of service in 2016

evidence.supports: the DNR plan to take towers out of service runs to 2016
evidence.quote: will be taken out of service in 2016

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin
DNR will discontinue fire towers in 2016

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WJFW says the 72 towers were decommissioned in 2015; the Sawyer County Record reports a DNR plan to take them out of service in 2016. Neither names a Menominee County tower, so the story reports both and does not link this tower to either.

notes_for_editor: Two lists place this tower and nothing else is documented: no build date, builder, fire history or owner. Cannot confirm whether it is one of the DNR's 72 towers. Needs a Menominee County history or Wisconsin AHI record and an owner check before any access or condition claim.
